title: what changing a habit of thought takes
subtitle: practice, patience, and no shortcuts

steps.prompt: what did putting a feeling into words seem to do?
steps.answer: it was linked with quieter amygdala activity. it can take a little edge off. it doesn't remove the feeling.

steps.text: a lesson can change what we understand. a habit changes when we do the thing again, many times.
which has changed more for you in the past?

options.label: understanding it
options.reply: that counts. understanding helps us know where to start.

options.label: doing it over and over
options.reply: that's how most habits settle in.

options.label: both, in turn
options.reply: yes. they seem to help each other.

steps.text: a review of 47 experiments found that big changes in people's intentions led to only small to medium changes in what they then did.
so knowing is a start. it's the repeating that carries it forward.
in a study of 96 people building a simple habit, it took a typical 66 days to feel automatic, and from 18 to 254 days between people.
steps.evidence: moderate (one study of simple habits, like drinking water; thoughts may differ)

steps.text: slow isn't a sign that anything is off. slow is how habits grow. in that study, missing a single day didn't undo it.
people may see promises online to rewire a brain in a week. nobody can honestly promise that, so hey you won't.

steps.prompt: what could make a small practice easier to repeat? pick any:
options: tying it to something i already do
doing it somewhere i'll see it
being easy on myself about days i skip
steps.reply: any of these can help. one is plenty.

steps.prompt: name a small practice you'd like to try:
ideas: one kind sentence after brushing my teeth.
naming one good thing at night.
one thing i like, written down.

steps.text: changing a habit of thought comes from repeating small things, and it's slower than most people expect. understanding alone doesn't carry it.
steps.evidence: moderate (one study of simple habits; thought habits may take their own time)

steps.text: pick one tiny practice from this path and tie it to something that already happens each day. try it for a week, and skip a day without any fuss.

grounding.idea: intentions change behavior only modestly; most of the work is in what's done afterward
simple habits took a median of 66 days to feel automatic, with wide variation
